lead: Two festas majors in a small, dense neighbourhood: the Eucharistic Congress estate and the houses of the indianos.
text: El Congrés was born in the 1950s: the Ros i de Ramis family sold 16.5 hectares of its Can Ros estate to the Patronato de Viviendas del Congreso Eucarístico (the Eucharistic Congress housing trust), the Church promoted the estate, designed by the architects Josep Soteras Mauri, Antoni Pineda and Carles Marquès, and the first homes were handed over in 1954. Els Indians recalls the Catalans who returned from the Americas after 1898 (the indianos) and built houses on unpopulated land; from that period the Torre Rosa, from 1920, survives. The partial plan for the estate was approved in February 1953 and the last block was finished in 1967-1968.

Each community has its own festival: els Indians, at the end of September, with references going back to the 1940s, lapsed during the dictatorship and was revived in 1983; and el Congrés, in the first week of October since 1986, in honour of Sant Pius X. Its axes are Plaça del Congrés Eucarístic and Plaça del Doctor Modrego, with the parish church of Sant Pius presiding over the first. With 15,254 inhabitants in 0.41 km², it has a density of 37,296 inhabitants/km², and it is a compact neighbourhood, with Congrés metro station on line 5 at street level. Its average sale price is 3,729 €/m². If you are selling, the average sale price is 8% above the Sant Andreu average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 298,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Sant Andreu (3rd of 7 by price). If you are investing, the average rent is in line with the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Blocks of an estate built between 1954 and 1968, and the odd indiano house such as the Torre Rosa.
